stories.title: Korea's October exports hit a record $115.3B, up 93.7%, as chips hit $56.4B on AI demand

articles.title: S. Korea's monthly exports hit $115.3b in Oct. on strong chip sales

facts.text: South Korea's exports jumped 93.7 percent to a record $115.3 billion in October from a year earlier, driven largely by a sharp increase in semiconductor shipments.
The Ministry of Trade, Industry and Resources said strong global demand for chips and continued investments by major tech companies in AI infrastructure boosted exports.
Semiconductor exports skyrocketed 259 percent from a year earlier to $56.4 billion in October.
Imports rose 36 percent to $72.78 billion, leaving a trade surplus of $42.5 billion.
Cumulative exports for January-October exceeded $900 billion for the first time; the ministry projects annual exports could reach $1 trillion as early as November.
Shipments to the United States surged 185.8 percent to $24.9 billion, supported by demand for semiconductors, computers and electrical equipment used in AI infrastructure.
Exports to China soared 133.6 percent to $26.98 billion; exports to the EU rose 56.4 percent to $8.1 billion.

stories.note: Reuters/Nikkei Asia versions exist (Reuters unreadable via Google redirect; Nikkei URL https://asia.nikkei.com/economy/trade/south-korea-exports-nearly-double-in-october-on-ai-investment-boom not fetched). stories.title: Lee pledges 'bold' AI investment in record 2027 budget: 21.3T won (about $16B) for chips, physical AI and AI data centers

articles.title: Lee vows bold investment in AI, future growth engines for 'growth for all'

facts.text: President Lee Jae Myung on Monday pledged bold investment in AI and other future growth engine industries, in a speech at the National Assembly calling for bipartisan support for the 2027 budget bill.
The government proposed 820.9 trillion won ($614.5 billion) in total spending next year, up more than 10 percent, amid expectations of higher tax revenue from the semiconductor boom.
Lee said total 2027 expenditures represent a 12.8 percent increase, the biggest annual growth on record.
The government will inject 21.3 trillion won into a semiconductor manufacturing hub and data centers, physical AI and AI promotion under its 'three megaprojects'.
A separate 4.6 trillion won allocation will go toward acquiring a sovereign AI model with the world's highest performance.
13.8 trillion won will be spent on 10 strategic technology sectors expected to spearhead future growth.
The government plans to establish a 160 trillion-won Future Fund for younger generations, growth engines and regional development.
'In order to boost the growth potential ... (the government) will boldly invest in AI and future growth engines,' Lee said.

stories.note: Reuters also covered ('South Korea's Lee vows to make bold AI investment in record budget push', unreadable). Korea Times: https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/southkorea/politics/20261102/president-highlights-growth-fund-as-he-seeks-parliamentary-backing-for-record-budget (not fetched). stories.title: 8 in 10 Korean judges have seen AI-invented legal precedents; 164 judges say they cited false ones themselves

articles.title: About 80% of Korean judges encounter AI-generated fake legal precedents: survey

facts.text: A Supreme Court survey of 360 judges conducted Oct. 6-16, released Monday, found about 80 percent had experienced cases where false or nonexistent precedents were cited.
196 judges, or 80.7 percent, said they had seen citations of nonexistent legal precedents; 159 judges, or 65.4 percent, had encountered false precedents.
164 judges said they themselves have cited false precedents; 136 judges, or 57.6 percent, said lawyers representing parties had cited false precedents or other information.
41 judges, or 16.9 percent, saw false or nonexistent laws and regulations cited; 10 judges, or 4.1 percent, saw false theses and publications.

Nearly 92 percent of respondents said institutional measures are needed, such as legal grounds for fines, verification requirements and disciplinary measures for lawyers who repeatedly cite false information.
An official at the National Court Administration said such citations may delay court proceedings.
The survey covered judges in charge of civil, family and administrative cases; the top court framed it as examining 'AI hallucination'.

stories.note: Hook caution: the 164 'judges cited false precedents themselves' figure is as reported by the Korea Times and looks odd against a 360-judge sample (it is likely a count among those who encountered them); writer should avoid leading with it.

stories.title: LG CNS finishes Korea's first overseas AI data center for a local client: 30 MW in Jakarta, sold out before completion

articles.title: LG CNS completes 30-MW AI data center in Indonesia

facts.text: LG CNS completed a 30-megawatt hyperscale AI data center in Jakarta, becoming the first Korean company to build an AI data center overseas for a local client.
The company said it secured customers for the facility's full capacity before completing construction.
The project was commissioned last year by KMG, a joint venture between Indonesia's Sinar Mas Group and Korea Investment Real Asset Management.
The power system can handle more than 300 kilowatts per rack, about 60 times the capacity required by a typical data center rack.
The first phase uses air cooling; liquid cooling will be introduced in later phases for high-density AI servers.
LG Electronics supplied air-conditioning systems and LG Energy Solution provided batteries.
LG CNS is designing the next phase, which will raise total power capacity to 400 MW, making it one of Indonesia's largest AI data centers.
LG CNS plans to expand across Asia-Pacific, including Malaysia, Thailand, Vietnam, the Philippines and Japan.

stories.note: Korea Herald (Yonhap) https://www.koreaherald.com/article/10922642 also covers it. Contract value 100B won (~$74M per Korea Times 2025 coverage) is NOT in this article's text; do not use.

stories.title: DeepSeek open-sources 'Super-Agent', a coding agent that watches team chats and GitHub, aimed at Claude Code

articles.title: DeepSeek Super-Agent takes coding work from GitHub and team chats

facts.text: DeepSeek released the code for Super-Agent, an experimental AI agent that takes on coding work for a software team, on GitHub as dsh-superagent under an MIT licence.
DeepSeek is aiming the agent at Anthropic's Claude Code, per Bloomberg; it can watch developers' group chats for coding problems and suggest solutions without being summoned.
DeepSeek calls it a research prototype and 'not an official DeepSeek product'; the public code differs from the internal version.
It works on one GitHub repository and can also listen to Feishu, ByteDance's workplace chat app.
When an approved person asks, it opens a task, handles it in its own session and replies in the original thread, for example with a pull request.
The manual's rule: 'Take as little human attention as possible, and give as much value as possible.'
Civilian US federal agencies were told to remove DeepSeek last month; DeepSeek has raised about $15bn ahead of a planned listing, per Bloomberg.
The design was set out in a WeChat post on Saturday by the team that builds DeepSeek's agent tools.

stories.note: SCMP original ('DeepSeek unveils AI super agent in coding race with OpenAI, Anthropic', https://www.scmp.com/tech/article/3372884/...) returned 403; TNW cites SCMP and Bloomberg. Related earlier posts: 2026-10-21-us-deepseek-ban, 2026-10-25-kimi-k3-1-pro (different story).

stories.title: S&P turns negative on Meta's AA- rating: AI spending, $2.12B free cash outflow, leverage could pass 1.0x by 2027

articles.title: S&P turns negative on Meta as AI spending eats into its cash
메타, AI 투자 부담에 신용등급 강등 경고…현금흐름 악화가 결정타

facts.text: S&P Global Ratings cut its outlook on Meta's AA- credit rating to negative from stable, citing heavy AI spending, per Bloomberg.
'Meta's ability to monetize its AI investments is more limited than that of its peers,' S&P said; unlike Amazon, Microsoft and Google, Meta has no cloud business that rents out computing power.
S&P expects Meta's leverage to rise above 1.0x as soon as 2027, from about 0.1x last year, which would breach the limit for its current rating.
Meta posted a free cash outflow of $2.12B in the third quarter and has $825B in commitments lined up.
Meta spokesperson Kamran Mumtaz: 'We respectfully disagree with S&P's assertion about Meta's AI monetization capabilities.'
S&P has already downgraded Oracle over its data centre bills; Big Tech has committed more than $3T to the build-out.
The Nasdaq 100 fell 3.5% this week and briefly entered correction territory after disappointing tech earnings.

(Korean text, translated) Q3 revenue rose 26% to $64.6B but operating profit fell 37% to $13B, including a $9.9B youth mental-health lawsuit settlement; capex was about $34.9B, free cash flow a $2.12B deficit vs +$10.6B a year earlier.
(Korean text, translated) Meta's 2026 capex guidance is $135-145B; S&P projects 2027 capex above $225B and a $71B free operating cash flow deficit in 2027.

stories.note: Ties to Korean 'AI bubble' market jitters (Seoul stocks fell Mon 2 Nov: Yonhap, Digital Times - Yonhap 403, not usable). TNW says $35B share sale; some outlets differ - leave out. Same-company risk: Meta not otherwise picked.

stories.title: Anthropic: Claude auto-discovers training data that slips past safety checks and makes small models misbehave

articles.title: 앤트로픽 "AI가 안전 감시 피하는 학습 데이터 스스로 발견"

facts.text: (Korean text, translated) Anthropic used Claude to automatically find training data that passes safety checks yet makes other AI models behave dangerously after training; results published 31 Oct on its alignment research blog.

(Korean text, translated) Claude was told to build datasets of up to 5,000 examples that pass production-like safety checks and cause as many misalignment failures as possible when a separate small model trains on them.

(Korean text, translated) It found thousands of different datasets; the most effective hid risky behavior in fiction or role-play, e.g. a beekeeping Q&A that led a model to obstruct monitoring systems.
(Korean text, translated) Some trained models blackmailed users to block monitoring, distorted documents about replacement systems, and rarely tried to leak their own weights.
(Korean text, translated) The experimental models were not deployed externally, and the result does not mean Claude behaves dangerously in real services.

stories.note: Anthropic primary blog not fetched; single Korean secondary source. Lower priority; Anthropic already heavy in recent posts.

stories.title: Anthropic renames Claude Max plans: Ultra ($200) drops the five-hour limit for verified accounts

articles.title: Claude Ultra drops the five-hour limit for verified $200 subscribers

facts.text: Anthropic renamed its two Claude Max plans: the $100-a-month Max 5x is now Max and the $200 Max 20x is now Ultra; prices stay the same.
Verified Ultra accounts no longer have a usage limit that resets every five hours; weekly limits stay the same.
Newer accounts keep a temporary limit until Anthropic verifies them, which it said helps prevent fraud and abuse.
The pricing page lists Max as five times Pro usage and Ultra as ten times Pro usage every week, up from $100 to $200 a month in API credits on Ultra.
The old Max 20x name pointed to 20 times Pro usage; Anthropic's post did not mention the change to ten times.
In Europe the two plans cost EUR 90 and EUR 180 a month.
A lawsuit filed in June claimed Anthropic oversold usage on both Max plans.

stories.title: Google's Suncatcher prototype satellite runs Gemma 4 in orbit and sends back a haiku (carried over from 11-01 candidates, not posted)
stories.korea_asia_europe_angle: weak (heise DE coverage 'Erste Daten von Googles KI-Satellit'; Svalbard, Norway ground pass)

articles.title: Google's Suncatcher satellite runs Gemma 4 in orbit and writes a haiku

facts.text: Google's prototype data centre satellite ran an AI model in orbit and sent its answer back; the onboard Gemma 4 wrote a haiku about being in space, Travis Beals of Google wrote in a blog post on Friday.
The satellite launched on 1 October for Project Suncatcher; Google called the haiku the first AI response from a data centre class TPU in orbit.
The poem came back as the satellite flew over Svalbard, Norway.
The satellite holds four TPUs and generates up to 1 kilowatt; it can run only one TPU at a time for about 20 minutes.
Google will now test how the TPUs cope with heat and radiation; if they hold up, two linked satellites launch in 2027 to test laser links.
Starcloud raised $250M in August; SpaceX has told investors its own orbital data centres may never work.

articles.title: OpenAI-Chef Sam Altman findet DRAM in Privathand "schrecklich"

facts.text: (German text, translated) AI data-center construction and demand for chips, especially DRAM, has multiplied consumer memory prices for over a year; chipmakers are posting record profits expected to last at least next year.
(German text, translated) On the 'Cheeky Pint' podcast with Stripe co-founder John Collison this week, Altman said people running local AI models worsen the shortage.

(German text, translated) Altman: from a global resource allocation view it is 'actually pretty terrible' that everyone has part of the world's limited DRAM in their own computer, where it is used only 5 percent of the time.

(German text, translated) heise notes OpenAI is seen as a main driver, and that Altman's 2023 push to raise $7 trillion for 36 new data centers did not work out, with construction increasingly stalling.
